metadata.title: Open RISC-V SoC Prototype
metadata.description: Start from the ISA contract; branch through architecture, RTL verification, physical implementation, and software integration; reunite in a bootable FPGA SoC prototype

domains.title: ISA and architecture
domains.description: Turn an instruction set into measurable microarchitectural and interconnect decisions

domains.title: RTL and verification
domains.description: Implement synthesizable hardware and establish simulation and formal evidence

domains.title: Physical implementation
domains.description: Carry the design from synthesis through timing, placement, routing, power, and signoff

domains.title: Software and integration
domains.description: Connect the toolchain, firmware, peripherals, FPGA validation, and reproducible delivery

nodes.title: RISC-V ISA contract
nodes.outcome: Read machine-level behavior from the unprivileged ISA and define an implementable RV32IM target
nodes.rationale: RTL cannot be reviewed coherently until supported instructions, traps, privilege assumptions, and architectural state are explicit

acceptance.title: ISA implementation matrix
acceptance.description: List every supported instruction and exception
criteria: Bind each item to an executable compliance test
Record every intentionally unsupported extension

frontiers.title: Profiles and platform contracts
frontiers.summary: Profiles are narrowing the gap between optional extensions and software-compatible platforms

frontiers.title: Vector cryptography
frontiers.summary: Ratified vector cryptography is bringing data-independent high-throughput primitives into the ISA

frontiers.title: Capability architectures
frontiers.summary: CHERI work is extending RISC-V with hardware-enforced memory capabilities

nodes.title: Pipeline microarchitecture
nodes.outcome: Specify a five-stage pipeline with hazards, bypassing, control recovery, and measurable performance
nodes.rationale: A block diagram is not a microarchitecture until timing, state transitions, conflicts, and recovery behavior are testable

acceptance.title: Cycle-accurate microarchitecture specification
acceptance.description: Define every pipeline register and control transfer
criteria: Provide hazard and forwarding tables
Predict CPI for at least three workloads

frontiers.title: Configurable application-class cores
frontiers.summary: Open cores such as CVA6 expose increasingly configurable pipelines and memory systems

frontiers.title: Composable generator ecosystems
frontiers.summary: Chipyard is making architectural exploration reproducible across generators and SoC configurations

frontiers.title: Profile-driven implementation
frontiers.summary: RISC-V profiles increasingly influence which architectural features must coexist

nodes.title: Memory-system architecture
nodes.outcome: Design caches, address maps, arbitration, buses, and peripheral attachment for a small SoC
nodes.rationale: A CPU becomes a system only when latency, ordering, backpressure, address ownership, and failure behavior are explicit

acceptance.title: Executable SoC memory map
criteria: Document arbitration and backpressure
Pass concurrent CPU and peripheral traffic tests

frontiers.title: Chiplet-aware interconnect
frontiers.summary: SoC composition is expanding from on-die buses toward interoperable die-to-die fabrics

frontiers.title: Coherent generator frameworks
frontiers.summary: Chipyard connects cores, caches, accelerators, and interconnect generators through reproducible configurations

frontiers.title: Capability-tagged memory
frontiers.summary: CHERI introduces metadata and checks that reshape cache and memory-system design

nodes.title: Synthesizable RTL
nodes.outcome: Write parameterized SystemVerilog with explicit sequential boundaries and synthesis-safe behavior
nodes.rationale: Code that simulates is not necessarily portable, synthesizable, reset-safe, or understandable during timing closure

acceptance.title: Lint-clean reusable RTL library
acceptance.description: Include registers, FIFOs, arbiters, and interfaces
criteria: Use one clocking convention and explicit reset policy
Synthesize every component without inferred latches

frontiers.title: Hardware compiler IR
frontiers.summary: CIRCT is introducing reusable compiler infrastructure between hardware languages and implementation tools

frontiers.title: Faster compiled simulation
frontiers.summary: Verilator continues to move large SystemVerilog designs into software-like compilation workflows

frontiers.title: Generator-based RTL
frontiers.summary: Chipyard demonstrates parameterized hardware generation beyond hand-written module copies

nodes.title: Simulation verification
nodes.outcome: Build self-checking unit and integration tests with assertions, coverage, and deterministic regressions
nodes.rationale: Waveform inspection cannot scale into evidence that corner cases, protocol rules, and recovery paths were exercised

acceptance.title: Reproducible verification regression
acceptance.description: Use scoreboards and executable reference models
criteria: Measure functional and structural coverage
Archive seeds, logs, and failing waveforms

frontiers.title: Python-native verification
frontiers.summary: cocotb is widening access to coroutine-based hardware verification and reusable software tooling

frontiers.title: Compiled simulation at scale
frontiers.summary: Verilator is improving language coverage and performance for large open hardware systems

frontiers.title: IR-level test generation
frontiers.summary: CIRCT is developing random-test and verification dialects above individual simulators

nodes.title: Formal properties
nodes.outcome: Prove control, protocol, and safety properties and distinguish assumptions from guarantees
nodes.rationale: Simulation samples executions; formal methods can exhaustively expose unreachable states, deadlocks, and missing environmental constraints

acceptance.title: Formal property suite
acceptance.description: Prove FIFO, arbiter, and pipeline safety properties
criteria: Cover at least one deep reachable behavior
Review every assumption for vacuous proofs

frontiers.title: IR-native bounded model checking
frontiers.summary: CIRCT is lowering verification problems through reusable dialects into SMT backends

frontiers.title: Open-source formal orchestration
frontiers.summary: SymbiYosys is integrating bounded, induction, cover, and liveness workflows

frontiers.title: Logical equivalence checking
frontiers.summary: CIRCT is exposing SMT-backed equivalence checks between hardware representations

nodes.title: Logic synthesis
nodes.outcome: Map RTL into a constrained gate-level netlist and explain area, timing, and inference results
nodes.rationale: Synthesis is the first place where coding style, constraints, libraries, and architecture become comparable implementation evidence

acceptance.title: Constrained synthesis report
acceptance.description: Reproduce the mapped netlist from one command
criteria: Explain the critical logic cones and inferred memories
Compare at least two architectural alternatives

frontiers.title: Compiler-based synthesis
frontiers.summary: CIRCT is adding reusable logic-synthesis passes and hardware-specific intermediate representations

frontiers.title: Open synthesis ecosystems
frontiers.summary: Yosys continues to connect front ends, technology mapping, formal tooling, and open PDK flows

frontiers.title: Automated PPA exploration
frontiers.summary: OpenROAD is targeting autonomous optimization across the RTL-to-GDSII flow

nodes.title: Detailed physical design
nodes.outcome: Create a floorplan, power grid, placement, clock tree, routing, and implementation report
nodes.rationale: A valid netlist is not a manufacturable layout until congestion, clocking, power delivery, geometry, and routing constraints converge

acceptance.title: Reproducible routed design
criteria: Close placement and routing without fatal violations
Archive metrics and implementation artifacts

frontiers.title: Autonomous RTL-to-GDSII
frontiers.summary: OpenROAD is integrating flow stages around no-human-in-loop implementation targets

frontiers.title: Distributed design-space search
frontiers.summary: Open implementation flows are using parallel exploration to trade runtime against PPA quality

frontiers.title: Reproducible physical-design CI
frontiers.summary: OpenROAD publishes regression infrastructure for implementation metrics and flow changes

nodes.title: Signoff closure
nodes.outcome: Constrain clocks and interfaces, analyze paths, repair violations, and defend final PPA tradeoffs
nodes.rationale: A routed design still fails if constraints are incomplete or if timing, slew, capacitance, clock skew, and power are not jointly reviewed

acceptance.title: Closure dossier
acceptance.description: Provide complete clock and interface constraints
criteria: Explain worst setup and hold paths
Track area, power, timing, and design-rule changes across iterations

frontiers.title: Metric-driven flow regression
frontiers.summary: OpenROAD regression infrastructure compares slack, area, skew, slew, capacitance, and routing outcomes

frontiers.title: Machine-guided flow tuning
frontiers.summary: OpenROAD is integrating modeling and prediction into implementation optimization

frontiers.title: Open static timing analysis
frontiers.summary: OpenSTA keeps timing models and constraint behavior inspectable inside an open implementation flow

nodes.title: Cross-toolchain
nodes.outcome: Compile, link, inspect, and debug bare-metal RISC-V programs against the implemented ISA contract
nodes.rationale: A processor is not usable until software flags, ABI, linker layout, startup code, and architectural features agree with hardware

acceptance.title: Reproducible RISC-V toolchain harness
acceptance.description: Build freestanding C and assembly programs
criteria: Inspect ELF sections and generated instructions
Fail the build when software requests an unsupported extension

frontiers.title: Profile-aware toolchains
frontiers.summary: RISC-V profiles are shaping portable compiler targets beyond individual extension flags

frontiers.title: Vector cryptography code generation
frontiers.summary: Compilers must map high-level cryptographic workloads onto new vector extension contracts

frontiers.title: Capability-aware compilation
frontiers.summary: CHERI requires compilers, ABIs, loaders, and hardware to preserve capability semantics together

nodes.title: Firmware integration
nodes.outcome: Bring up startup code, interrupts, timers, UART, memory layout, and a minimal RTOS environment
nodes.rationale: Firmware exposes integration failures that isolated CPU and peripheral tests cannot reveal

acceptance.title: Automated firmware bring-up suite
acceptance.description: Boot from reset into a diagnostic application
criteria: Exercise interrupts, timer, UART, and memory boundaries
Capture cycle-accurate failure evidence in simulation

frontiers.title: Portable RTOS hardware descriptions
frontiers.summary: Zephyr is expanding declarative board, device-tree, driver, and architecture integration

frontiers.title: Security-root integration
frontiers.summary: OpenTitan demonstrates coordinated ROM, lifecycle, key management, and hardware security blocks

frontiers.title: Capability-aware system software
frontiers.summary: CHERI research is moving memory protection into toolchain, ABI, kernel, and hardware contracts

nodes.title: FPGA SoC prototype
nodes.outcome: Deliver one reproducible FPGA image that boots software and carries architecture, verification, and implementation evidence
nodes.rationale: The final prototype must reunite every branch; otherwise the learning path proves isolated exercises rather than system engineering

acceptance.title: Audited RISC-V SoC prototype
acceptance.description: Build bitstream and firmware from a clean checkout
criteria: Boot diagnostics and a small application on hardware
Publish ISA, verification, timing, and known-limit reports together

frontiers.title: Open silicon reference systems
frontiers.summary: OpenTitan is integrating reusable IP, verification, firmware, security, and implementation documentation

frontiers.title: Generator-to-prototype continuity
frontiers.summary: Chipyard links configurable hardware generators with simulation and FPGA-oriented system flows

frontiers.title: Continuous hardware delivery
frontiers.summary: OpenROAD regression practices are moving implementation artifacts and PPA metrics into repeatable CI

bridges.reason: Microarchitecture choices must survive synthesized PPA evidence
Firmware bring-up depends on verified CPU and peripheral behavior

provenance.sourcePolicy: Official technical documentation, standards, complete courses, whole-resource assignments, and link-only public evidence
